subject.title: [Bug]: GitHub Copilot anthropic-messages transport silently hangs ~365s in isolated cron sessions (2026.5.27)

question: When a GitHub Copilot Claude `anthropic-messages` isolated run aborts with no assistant text, no tool metadata, and no timeout flags, should OpenClaw retry/fallback automatically or surface the abort as terminal?
rationale: Current source proves the remaining gap, but safe behavior depends on maintainer policy because fallback after an aborted agent run can repeat side effects unless the no-output/no-tool state is treated as replay-safe.

options.title: Define replay-safe fallback
options.body: Treat aborted no-output/no-tool Copilot Claude runs as fallback-worthy only after live proof and focused tests show no committed work can be duplicated.

options.title: Transport-first repair only
options.body: Fix the Copilot Anthropic stream to emit progress or first-token idle errors, and keep aborted run fallback conservative.

options.title: Keep terminal abort behavior
options.body: Document that these aborts surface as cron errors and require operators to choose a different primary transport or explicit retry policy.

recommendation.title: Define replay-safe fallback
recommendation.body: Treat aborted no-output/no-tool Copilot Claude runs as fallback-worthy only after live proof and focused tests show no committed work can be duplicated.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant current history is concentrated in GitHub Copilot provider metadata/stream code and adjacent fallback-classifier work.
